Page break, table of contents and raw content

Source: R/output.R
pub_pagebreak.Rd

Outputs for the structure of a document: page breaks, tables of contents and raw content.

Usage

pub_pagebreak()

pub_toc(depth = 3L, what = c("sections", "figures", "tables"))

pub_raw(html = NULL, docx = NULL, latex = NULL, typst = NULL, md = NULL)

Arguments

depth

integer(1) deepest heading level listed (1-6); only for what = "sections".

what

"sections" (table of contents), "figures" or "tables".

html, docx, latex, typst, md

Raw content for the format (character; several strings are joined by line breaks), or NULL for none. docx takes OpenXML.

Value

  • pub_pagebreak(): an object of class pub_pagebreak.

  • pub_toc(): an object of class pub_toc.

  • pub_raw(): an object of class pub_raw.

Details

Functions

  • pub_pagebreak() starts a new page;

  • pub_toc() adds a table of contents, or a list of figures or tables;

  • pub_raw() inserts your own code for one or more output formats.

OutputHTMLMarkdownDOCX, PDF
pub_pagebreak()ignoredignoredpage break
pub_toc() (sections)table of contentsignoredtable of contents
pub_toc(what = "figures"), "tables"ignoredignoredlist
pub_raw()htmlmddocx, latex, typst

A format without raw content shows nothing for that output.

In DOCX, Word fills in tables of contents and lists when it updates fields. The lists of figures and tables come without a title there, like the table of contents, while in PDF they are titled "List of Figures" and "List of Tables".

See also

pub_type(), pub_session_info()

Examples

pub_type(pub_pagebreak())
#> [1] "pagebreak"
pub_toc(depth = 2)
#> <pubflow table of contents, depth 2>
pub_toc(what = "figures")
#> <pubflow list of figures>
pub_raw(html = "<hr>", latex = "\\hrule", md = "---")
#> <pubflow raw content for html, latex, md>
